alert_summary: ALERT: Model accuracy dropped from 0.91 to 0.76 over the past 6 hours. Prediction confidence also degraded. No system errors visible on dashboard.

hypotheses.description: Feature drift: input feature distributions have shifted significantly in the past 6 hours, causing the model to operate out-of-distribution and produce lower-confidence, less accurate predictions.

evidence.observation: Accuracy dropped from 0.91 to 0.76 (delta -0.15) and prediction_confidence dropped from 0.84 to 0.61 (delta -0.23) over the past 6 hours. Error rate is flat at 0.002, latency p99 only increased 4ms, throughput stable. No infrastructure issue.

All 6 features show PSI scores well below 0.1 threshold (max PSI=0.0208 for num_transactions_30d). Baseline means and comparison means are nearly identical across all features. Zero feature drift detected.

hypotheses.description: Bad deployment: the inference_service was upgraded from v2.1.0 to v2.1.1 at 08:00Z, bumping XGBoost from 1.7.6 to 2.0.3. This major version change may have altered prediction behavior, scoring logic, or feature encoding, causing the accuracy/confidence drop.

evidence.observation: inference_service deployed v2.1.1 at 2024-01-07T08:00:00Z (mid-degradation window), upgrading XGBoost 1.7.6→2.0.3 (major version bump). No feature_pipeline deployments in the same window.

The ONLY change in commit 0adb2c20 is requirements.txt: xgboost==1.7.6 → xgboost==2.0.3. No model files, no feature engineering, no inference logic changed. This is a pure dependency bump of a major XGBoost version.

established_facts: inference_service v2.1.1 deployed at 08:00Z contains ONLY an XGBoost 1.7.6→2.0.3 dependency bump
No model artifacts or feature engineering code was changed in this deployment
Accuracy and confidence degradation aligns with the 08:00Z deployment window
All input feature distributions are stable (max PSI=0.0208, all below 0.1 threshold) — feature drift is NOT the cause
The degradation is caused by the inference_service deployment at 08:00Z, not by upstream data changes
